name: Motion Blur Direction
description: Analyzes motion blur directionality to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
algorithm: Motion Blur Direction — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes motion blur direction consistency for video forensic detection:

1. **Motion Blur Detection**: Blurred regions in each frame are identified by analyzing the directional spread of the local point spread function (PSF). Motion-blurred regions show characteristic elongated PSFs in the direction of motion.

2. **Blur Direction Estimation**: For each blurred region, the blur direction and magnitude are estimated. Natural motion blur direction should be consistent with the object's motion vector between adjacent frames — blur direction aligns with the displacement vector.

3. **Global-Local Blur Consistency**: Camera motion produces globally coherent blur (all objects blur in the same direction, adjusted for depth). Object motion produces local blur. The method verifies that the observed blur field is consistent with a combination of camera and object motion. Composited or generated content may show inconsistent blur directions between regions.

4. **Face-Background Blur Coherence**: When camera motion occurs, the face and background should show consistent motion blur. Deepfake composites may show the face with different blur than the background — either sharper (generated without blur accounting) or blurred differently (incorrect motion estimation).

5. **Temporal Blur Continuity**: Motion blur should vary smoothly across frames — increasing with faster motion, decreasing with slower motion. The method tracks blur magnitude and direction temporally. Abrupt changes in blur characteristics without corresponding motion changes indicate manipulation or generation artifacts.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through motion blur direction analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
